study_identification.author_journal_year: Segal et al., Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging, 2025
study_identification.title: Multiscale Heterogeneity of White Matter Morphometry in Psychiatric Disorders

study_characteristics.study_objective: To quantify multiscale heterogeneity of white matter volume (WMV) deviations in six psychiatric disorders using normative modeling, and test whether heterogeneous voxel-level deviations aggregate within common tracts, regions, and large-scale networks.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Group comparisons of deviation burden (cases vs held-out controls) using nonparametric rank-sum tests; spatial overlap differences tested via permutation (10,000 permutations) with FDR correction using PALM; multiscale analyses across voxels, tracts, regions, and networks.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Voxel-level WMV deviations are highly heterogeneous across individuals; ASD and SCZ show aggregation of negative deviations into common tracts/regions/networks, whereas other disorders show limited aggregation.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Fewer than ~8% of individuals with the same diagnosis share deviations at the same voxel. ASD and SCZ exhibited higher median extreme negative deviation burden than held-out controls (p < .001), and aggregation into common tracts/regions/networks was observed in up to ~69% of individuals. Case–control differences in other disorders were limited (see Table 2 and Supplementary Tables).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Per-diagnosis demographic details are not consistently reported across aggregated datasets; cross-sectional design limits causal inference; tractography-based mapping required an independent HCP cohort due to variable DWI availability in clinical samples; potential residual heterogeneity across sites/datasets despite covariate adjustment.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Introduces a multiscale framework (voxel→tract→region→network) for WMV deviation heterogeneity; uses likelihood warping and B-splines in normative modeling; evaluates site residuals via SVM; applies permutation-based overlap inference with FDR; uses independent HCP DWI for circuit mapping.

general_notes.general_notes: Datasets referenced include: ABIDE I (Di Martino et al., 2014); ABIDE II (Di Martino et al., 2017); Australian Schizophrenia Research Bank (Loughland et al., 2010); OpenNeuro ds000212; OpenNeuro ds002748; and multiple single-site clinical cohorts cited in Table 1 of the main paper. Total datasets=14 across 25 scan sites.
